name: Sample questions (for testing)
description: A small built-in sample covering every question type. Disable it in the Question Bank Manager once you add your own banks.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle was discovered by James Chadwick in 1932?
questions.explanation: Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles and detected a neutral, penetrating radiation: the neutron.

questions.question: Write the electron configuration (s, p notation) of a sodium atom.
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹. The outer 3s electron is easily lost to form Na⁺.

questions.question: Which statements are true of isotopes of the same element? Select all that apply.
options: They have the same number of protons
They have different numbers of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have the same chemical properties
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ. Chemical properties depend on electron arrangement, which is the same.

questions.question: Arrange these elements in order of increasing first ionisation energy.
questions.explanation: Ionisation energy generally rises across a period, but Al is lower than Mg: aluminium’s outer electron is in a 3p sublevel, which is higher in energy and shielded by the full 3s sublevel.

questions.question: A sample of chlorine is 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37. Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine.
How many moles are in 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Mr = 40)
questions.explanation: moles = mass ÷ Mr = 4.0 ÷ 40 = 0.10 mol

questions.question: What volume does 0.5 mol of an ideal gas occupy at s.t.p.?
questions.explanation: One mole of gas occupies 22.4 L at s.t.p., so 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 L.

questions.question: What is the value of the Avogadro constant?
questions.explanation: The Avogadro constant, L, is 6.0 × 10²³ mol⁻¹: the number of particles in one mole.

questions.question: Match each quantity with its unit.
questions.explanation: Molar mass is grams per mole, concentration is moles per litre, amount of substance is measured in moles, and one mole of gas occupies 22.4 L at s.t.p.

questions.question: What is the empirical formula of glucose, C6H12O6?
questions.explanation: Divide each subscript by the highest common factor, 6: C₆H₁₂O₆ → CH₂O.

questions.question: Which functional group is present in ethanoic acid, CH3COOH?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group, –COOH.

questions.question: Give the IUPAC name of CH3CH2OH.
questions.explanation: Two carbons (eth-), single bonds only (-an-), and an –OH group (-ol): ethanol.

questions.question: Which of these are addition reactions? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: In addition reactions two molecules join to form one, typically across a C=C double bond. Chlorination of methane is substitution; dehydration of ethanol is elimination.

questions.question: Arrange these alkanes in order of increasing boiling point.
questions.explanation: Boiling point rises with chain length because larger molecules have stronger van der Waals forces between them.

questions.question: Match each reaction type with an example.
questions.explanation: Substitution swaps one atom for another; addition joins molecules across a double bond; elimination removes a small molecule to form a double bond; oxidation of ethanol to ethanal (acidified Na₂Cr₂O₇) is a redox reaction.

questions.question: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
options: It raises the temperature of the reactants
It provides a pathway with a lower activation energy
It increases the concentration of the reactants
It shifts the equilibrium to the right
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, so a greater fraction of collisions are effective. It is not used up.

questions.question: Which changes would increase the rate of reaction between marble chips and hydrochloric acid? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature, higher concentration and greater surface area (smaller pieces) all increase the rate. Larger chips have less surface area, so the reaction is slower.

questions.question: In a reaction, 60 cm3 of oxygen was collected in the first 2 minutes. Calculate the average rate in cm3 s-1.
questions.explanation: 2 minutes = 120 s. Average rate = 60 cm³ ÷ 120 s = 0.5 cm³ s⁻¹.

questions.question: Name the catalyst used in the mandatory experiment on the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.
questions.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide (manganese dioxide, MnO₂) catalyses 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂.

questions.question: The same mass of marble reacts with excess dilute HCl. Order these forms from slowest to fastest reaction.
questions.explanation: Smaller particles have a greater total surface area, so more collisions occur per second and the reaction is faster.
